merge_request.title: Gate CVS advisory scanner findings on the scanning license
merge_request.description:
## What

Gate the public continuous-vulnerability-scanning (CVS) advisory scanner, `Gitlab::VulnerabilityScanning::AdvisoryScanner`, on the per-project scanning licensed feature. CVS findings are now only created for Ultimate-eligible projects.

## Why

`AdvisoryScanner#cvs_enabled_for_project?` previously checked only the per-project CVS setting (`cvs_for_dependency_scanning_enabled` / `cvs_for_container_scanning_enabled`), which defaults on. This allowed any project with the setting enabled to receive CVS findings regardless of license tier. CVS findings are Ultimate-only, so the license check was missing.

## Behaviour

- **Ultimate projects**: no change. The licensed feature is available, so the gate passes.
- **Non-Ultimate projects**: will no longer receive CVS findings from this path. Per the Ultimate-only intent of CVS, they should not have been receiving them; this is a correctness fix.
- This path is not behind a feature flag and is live default-on, so the behaviour change ships immediately. A feature flag could be added if the CVS owners prefer a gradual rollout. A changelog entry (type: fixed) is included.

## Related

- Companion to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/249075 (malware CVS gate)
- Gap surfaced in review of that MR by @hbakergitlab

## Tests

`ee/spec/lib/gitlab/vulnerability_scanning/advisory_scanner_spec.rb` now stubs `dependency_scanning` and `container_scanning` availability. A "not licensed" context has been added under both the Dependency Scanning and Container Scanning blocks, asserting no vulnerabilities are created when the licensed features are unavailable.

commits.title: Stub licensed features in the cvs_enabled_for_project? spec
commits.message:
Stub licensed features in the cvs_enabled_for_project? spec

The new licensed_feature_available? gate in cvs_enabled_for_project?
returns false unless the project is licensed, but the unit describe
only set the CVS settings and never granted the licence, so its
expected: true rows failed in CI. Stub dependency_scanning and
container_scanning there too, matching the #execute describe, so the
rows exercise the setting logic with the licence present.

commits.title: Gate CVS advisory scanner findings on the scanning license
commits.message:
Gate CVS advisory scanner findings on the scanning license

Continuous vulnerability scanning (CVS) findings are Ultimate-only, but
AdvisoryScanner#cvs_enabled_for_project? only checked the per-project
CVS setting, not the license -- so any project with the setting on could
get findings regardless of tier. Gate per purl type on
licensed_feature_available?(:container_scanning / :dependency_scanning),
mirroring cvs_for_container_scanning_available and
cvs_for_dependency_scanning_available.

Companion to the malware CVS gate in
https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/249075; raised in
review by `@hbakergitlab`.

Changelog: fixed
EE: true
